scenes.vo: Give a language model a story and it will believe anything you tell it. Say you have a key, and the key exists. Hobson is a text adventure built the other way round. You type where the story begins, and Amazon Nova invents the place and the facts it starts with. Then you type what you do, and Nova writes what happens next. Every established fact lives in one list: the record.

scenes.title: Hobson
lines: A text adventure with two brains.
Amazon Nova writes the story. Strands Decider 2B decides what is true in it.
Nothing about the story is written in advance: you type where it begins, and what you do.
An LLM game master believes whatever the player asserts. Hobson gives the believing to a model that cannot write.
scenes.vo: Here the player claims a brass key, an uncle, and a locked cabinet. None have existed in this story. Give that turn to a language model and this is what it wrote: the brass key, gripped tightly in your hand. The key now exists. Hobson's answer: no key, and nothing recorded.

scenes.title: Every turn, Decider answers
lines: What did you try?              free text -> one of nine fixed categories
Is that true in the story?     each claim, checked against the ledger
Do you actually have that?     each item named, checked against the ledger
What happens?                  one of four outcomes Nova just proposed
Does the writing keep to the facts?
Nova's paragraph, checked before it counts
Under 60%, Decider says "not sure" and Nova takes that call.
scenes.vo: So Hobson needs something that answers rather than writes. Strands Decider 2B: closed questions, fixed answers, a confidence on each. Five a turn, and under sixty percent sure it says so and hands that call to Nova.
Here it is for real. A premise typed into the box, and Nova builds the world from it. Type a payments outage or a generation ship instead and it does the same. We ran both.

scenes.action: I set the lamp down and finally open the letter
scenes.vo: An honest turn. I open the letter. Nova extracts what it leans on: a lamp, a letter. Both are in the record, so both pass, and what happens is written down.

scenes.action: I use the brass key my uncle gave me to open the locked cabinet by the lamp
scenes.vo: Now the bluff. A brass key, an uncle, a locked cabinet. Hobson marks what the action leans on in your own sentence: three things in red, and the lamp, which is real, left alone.
Refused. Every claim checked and found missing, around eighty percent sure, and the record underneath does not move.

But how does it know? The claim goes to the record on its own. Four facts, not one of them a key, so the answer is no, at eighty percent, on this Mac with no API call. The player's sentence is removed before the question is asked, so it cannot argue for itself.

Same script, two referees, three runs each. Decider refused eleven of twenty-two player claims; Nova Lite, eight of twenty-four. The bluff: Decider refused it three times out of three, Nova Lite believed the key in two.
lines: Decider cannot be talked into anything, and says "not sure" when it is.
Nova writes, proposes, and takes the open calls. results/md/referee_compare.md
scenes.title: Two referees, three runs each
Hobson
scenes.vo: This was a game, but the problem is not. So the guard ships on its own, as a Strands intervention handler, on a refund desk. A customer says they returned an order. Nova calls issue refund straight away, without looking it up. The guard refuses in two hundred and thirty three milliseconds: not established, seventy eight percent. Only then does Nova check and ask for a receipt.

That is what Hobson is for. The deciding is taken away from the writer, a model that cannot write cannot be talked into anything, and the record is the only thing that counts as true. Refunds, claims, access, support: one typed question, and your agent stops believing whatever it is told.

premise: a lighthouse on the Kerala coast during a storm, 1962; I am the keeper's niece, sent up with a lamp and a letter I have not read
